text.p: Santander Investment said it had it had downgraded Colombia's leading supermarket chain, Carulla to underperform because of disappointing 1996 earnings and an increasingly competitive food retailing environment.

It also said it was cutting its 1997 and 1998 earnings per share estimates by 14 percent and 16 percent respectively, following a 30 percent drop in the company's 1996 earnings year-to-year. "Since we initiated coverage on the stock with a Market Perform rating in September 1996, the orfinary shares have fallen by 36 percent," Santander said.

"Both the ordinary shares and the ADRs are now trading at a 52-week low and significantly below the ADR issue price of $1.33. Despite attractive valuations, we believe that Carulla is finding it increasingly difficult to maintain market share in an increasingly competitive market," it said.
It added that Santander had sharply cut its peso target price for Carulla's locally-traded shares from 7,130 to 3,000.
